sections.heading: What Kolto Labs is
sections.body:
Kolto Labs is an independent, non-commercial fan project. We build tools for *Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic* and *Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords*.

Our main project is **Project Telos**: KotOR in your browser, with a library of mods and extensions, a full debugger and TAS tools. It's in development and not open to the public yet. You bring your own copy of the game.

We also release smaller tools. **kq** lets you query a game install from the command line, and `kotor-formats` is a set of shared Rust libraries for the games' file formats. Both are released.

The name comes from kolto, the healing medium harvested in the oceans of Manaan. The games are more than twenty years old, and people still mod them.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.body:
Keep the games moddable for the next twenty years.

Project Telos is meant to give modders one place to publish and players one place to run mods. The plan is for mods to run in the browser, so a modder's files stay under their control and players get updates without reinstalling. We also want the games on phones, tablets and TVs. None of that works yet.

The tools under it follow one rule: load a file, save it unchanged, get the same bytes back. Parsers are strict by default and lenient only when you ask.

sections.heading: How we work
sections.body:
- Each released project has one repository, under [github.com/kolto-labs](https://github.com/kolto-labs).
- Bugs and feature requests go in public issues.

sections.heading: Standing on prior work
sections.body:
The games never shipped with public documentation or an official modding toolset. Modders mapped the engine themselves, and that work produced TSLPatcher, KotOR Tool, DeNCS and two decades of mods. We build on it and credit it.

We work with games we own. We never commit game assets or original executables. Project Telos doesn't include the game either: you link your own copy from Steam, GOG or Amazon, or upload your own files.

sections.heading: Not affiliated
sections.body: We're not affiliated with Lucasfilm, BioWare, Obsidian or the games' publishers. Is it legal? Yes. We build interoperable tools for games people already own, and we ship none of the games' content.

projects.name: kq
projects.tagline: Query a KotOR installation like it was plain text.
projects.description: kq is a command-line tool, separate from Project Telos. kq treats a KotOR or TSL game folder as structured, searchable data. It reads the archives in place, so nothing gets extracted first. Questions work the way rg works on a source tree and jq works on JSON. Start with kq which: every copy of a resource in engine resolve order, with a star on the copy the game actually loads.
features: which: every copy of a resource in engine resolve order (Override, modules, BIFs), with the loaded copy starred
cat: GFF, 2DA, TLK, SSF, NCS (decompiled to NSS), MDL, walkmeshes and more as an outline, gron lines, JSON or raw bytes
grep: regex search over decoded contents; hits are field paths, not byte offsets
delta, patch and merge: structural diffs and three-way merges of decoded resources
graph: an inventory of used, unused and overshadowed resources in an install
JSON and JSONL output plus stable exit codes, so scripts can branch on results
Works on a full install, a single module, or a folder of loose files

install.powershell: powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "Set-Item Env:KQ_REPO kolto-labs/kq; irm https://github.com/kolto-labs/kq/releases/download/v0.3.0/install.ps1 | iex"

projects.name: kotor-formats
projects.tagline: One copy of the byte layouts, so a patcher, a compiler and a query tool cannot drift apart.
projects.description: Three tools were each carrying their own copy of the KotOR I and II byte layouts, free to drift apart. These Rust crates are the one copy they all read from. Small on purpose, so each tool takes only what it needs: kotor-ncs-isa (the NCS instruction set as data), kotor-ncs (NCS read/write plus a decompiler built on the DeNCS algorithm), kotor-formats (GFF, 2DA, TLK, SSF, ERF/RIM) and kotor-diff (structural comparison).
features: Byte-exact round trips: type tags, field widths, raw labels and padding are preserved, not normalised
Lossless text: a total Latin-1 mapping, so encode(decode(x)) == x for all 256 byte values
Strict by default, accepting what TSLPatcher accepted; opt-in leniency for read-only tools
Errors in the (GFF-1) / (2DA-8) form mod authors already know from install logs
Early: the API is not stable yet, so depend on a git tag

faq.q: What is Kolto Labs?
faq.a: An independent group building tools for KotOR I and II. Our main project is Project Telos: KotOR in your browser, with mods, a debugger and TAS tools. It's in development. Released so far are the kq query tool and the kotor-formats libraries, on GitHub under github.com/kolto-labs.

faq.q: What is Project Telos?
faq.a: Our main project. It's KotOR I and II in your browser, with a library of mods and extensions, a full debugger and TAS tools. It's in development and not open to the public yet. The goal is one place for modders to publish and for players to run mods, with updates that don't need a reinstall.

faq.q: Is this legal?
faq.a: Yes. We build interoperable tools for games people already own. Our repositories contain no game assets and no copyrighted game code, and our tools need your own legally obtained copy of the games to do anything.

faq.q: Are you affiliated with Lucasfilm, Disney, BioWare, Obsidian, Aspyr or Saber?
faq.a: No. Kolto Labs is an independent, non-commercial community project, and none of those companies endorse or sponsor it. We have no information about any official Star Wars game, including the announced remake. Our work targets the original games.

faq.q: Where do I get the games?
faq.a: Buy them. Both games are sold on current PC storefronts, and your old discs work too. We don't help with, link to or answer questions about pirated copies.

faq.q: Can I play KOTOR in the browser today?
faq.a: Not yet. Project Telos is in development. The "Play in your browser" button goes to a page that explains what to expect, and it will open the game once there is something to open.

faq.q: Where does the game come from?
faq.a: From you. Project Telos doesn't include the game. You'll link a copy you own from Steam, GOG or Amazon, which is the way we recommend, or upload your own game files. Both are planned and neither is open yet.

faq.q: Will it run on my phone, tablet or TV?
faq.a: That's planned. Project Telos is built for the browser, and we want it on phones, tablets and TVs. None of those work yet.

faq.q: Which versions of the games do your tools support?
faq.a: Depends on the tool. kq and the format libraries read the games' data files, so they work with any install that has the standard layout. Project Telos and Hyperstim aren't out yet.

faq.q: When is Hyperstim coming out?
faq.a: When it's done. It's in development and built by volunteers. Watch the roadmap.

faq.q: Is Hyperstim a new engine, a remake or an emulator?
faq.a: No. It's built for the original games.

faq.q: How do I install kq?
faq.a:
kq is a command-line tool, separate from Project Telos. Run the installer for your system.

```sh
# macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://github.com/kolto-labs/kq/releases/download/v0.3.0/install.sh | KQ_REPO=kolto-labs/kq sh
```

```powershell
# Windows
powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "Set-Item Env:KQ_REPO kolto-labs/kq; irm https://github.com/kolto-labs/kq/releases/download/v0.3.0/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Or build it with Cargo:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/kolto-labs/kq --locked
```

Plain `cargo install kq` won't work, because the kq name on crates.io belongs to an unrelated tool.

faq.q: Does kq replace KotOR Tool, TSLPatcher or the other editors and patchers?
faq.a: No. kq is a command-line query tool: it lists, resolves, prints, searches and diffs. It doesn't edit archives, compile scripts or install mods. Use it for investigating and analyzing the game's files and content.

faq.q: Do you use decompiled game code?
faq.a: Not in the libraries or tools. Details are in our reverse-engineering policy.

faq.q: Why Rust?
faq.a: Parsing files from strangers' mods is exactly where memory safety pays off, and Rust gives us single static binaries, good cross-platform tooling and fast tests.

faq.q: Will Hyperstim or Adrenal trip my antivirus?
faq.a: Possibly. Antivirus scanners are wary of game add-ons.

faq.q: Is there a Discord or forum?
faq.a: Basically nowhere. This is a fan project that adheres to the aesthetic of my own personal nostalgia from the 2000s era.

faq.q: Do you take donations?
faq.a: We aren't set up to. The most useful thing you can give us is a bug report with steps to reproduce it.

faq.q: How can I help?
faq.a: Spread the word and link us. Our home is [github.com/kolto-labs](https://github.com/kolto-labs).

faq.q: Why is it called Kolto Labs?
faq.a: Kolto is the healing medium in KotOR, the stuff harvested on Manaan. That's basically what these projects do to an old engine: patch it, heal it, extend it. So I named it after kolto, and the rest followed the theme: Hyperstim, Adrenal, and release channels named after medpacs. Project Telos takes its name from the restoration effort in KotOR II.

join.intro: Kolto Labs is built by volunteers. Open an issue, send a pull request, or pick up something labelled good first issue.

lookingFor.detail: Comfortable in 32-bit x86 and MSVC-era C++, with Ghidra, IDA or a debugger.
You like binary formats, property tests and byte-exact round trips. kq and kotor-formats both have open issues.
You know what the vanilla command set can't do. Help shape Hyperstim so it makes sense to the people who'll use it.
Help shape Adrenal's API and its error messages.
Write tests that pin down engine behaviour and catch regressions in tools and mods.
Write specifications and guides for Ahto.
ASCII/ANSI art, pixel fonts, chiptune. Original work only, under an open license.
Tell us what differs between the disc, Steam, GOG and other builds.

steps: Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/kolto-labs/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [reverse-engineering policy](/join/#re-policy). They're short.
Find something to do: a good first issue, a bug you've hit, or a gap in the docs.
Comment on the issue so nobody duplicates your work.
Fork, branch, keep the change focused. Add or update tests.
Open a pull request. CI runs, and review happens in public.
join.rePolicy:
**Short version.** We reverse-engineer games we own, for interoperability, preservation and modding, and we keep our repositories clean.

- **Never commit** game assets, original executables, extracted game files, or anything from leaked or confidential material. Test fixtures are synthetic or generated.
- **Write your own code.** Don't paste disassembler or decompiler output into our repositories.
- **Conflicts of interest.** If you've had access to confidential source or documentation for these games, or work under an NDA that covers them, tell us before contributing to affected areas.
join.conduct:
We follow the [Contributor Covenant 2.1](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/).

- Be kind. Critique code and ideas, not people.
- Assume good faith, and ask before you assume.
- Newcomers are welcome. There are no stupid questions about a twenty-year-old undocumented engine.
- No harassment, personal attacks or discrimination, in our spaces or aimed at people in them.
- Don't publish anyone's private information.

Reports go to the maintainers privately and are handled in confidence. Enforcement follows the Covenant's guidelines, from a private warning up to a permanent ban.

communities.name: Deadly Stream
communities.why: Where KotOR modding lives: files, forums, works in progress, and a culture that takes credit and permissions seriously.

communities.name: LucasForums Archive Project
communities.why: For keeping the modding boards where most of the original KotOR tools and knowledge were built.

communities.name: KOTOR Community Portal
communities.why: Curated mod builds. A lot of players learned how to mod these games properly from them.

communities.name: r/kotor
communities.why: Twenty years on and still arguing about Revan. Long may it continue.

communities.name: Nexus Mods
communities.why: A second home for KotOR and TSL mods, and for the people who make them.

communities.name: NWNX
communities.why: The Neverwinter Nights extender community showed how far a script extender on a BioWare engine can go.

communities.name: The decompilation community
communities.why: decomp.dev, decomp.me, Decompedia and the teams behind them showed that matching decompilation of a whole game is achievable, and that progress can be public.

priorArt.name: TSLPatcher
priorArt.why: The installer most KotOR mods ship with. kotor-formats is strict by default and accepts what TSLPatcher accepts.

priorArt.name: nwnnsscomp
priorArt.why: Torlack's NWScript compiler from Neverwinter Nights. Modified builds of it still compile KotOR scripts, and TSLPatcher ships with one.

priorArt.name: KotOR Tool
priorArt.why: An editor for 2DA tables, scripts, templates and modules. Fred Tetra started it to experiment with 2DA files and scripts.

priorArt.name: DeNCS
priorArt.why: Turns compiled NCS scripts back into NSS source. JdNoa wrote the decompiler and Dashus the interface. The decompiler in kotor-ncs builds on its algorithm.

priorArt.name: MDLOps and kotorblender
priorArt.by: Chuck Chargin Jr., ndix UR and seedhartha
priorArt.why: [MDLOps](https://deadlystream.com/files/file/779-mdlops/) converts KotOR's binary models to text and back. Chuck Chargin Jr. wrote it and ndix UR took it to 1.0. kotorblender imports and exports the same models in Blender. It is a fork of Purifier and ndix UR's KotORBlender, which grew out of Symmetric's NeverBlender.

priorArt.name: K1SE and K2SE
priorArt.why: Script extenders that add new NWScript functions to the Steam builds of KotOR and TSL. [K1SE](https://deadlystream.com/topic/12324-resourcekotor-script-extender-k1sekse-100zip/) is on Deadly Stream and K2SE is on GitHub.
